title: Garden Birds — 2026-07-29
style: A landscape hanging composed of uneven vertical raffia falls, braided palm-rib rails, stitched indigo cotton panels and suspended bird-oracle clusters. Forms should be simplified into crests, breast patches, wings, tails and beaks using shells, beads, seed pods and metal discs. Use negative space between hanging columns so the artwork breathes. Edges should be fringed, knotted and imperfect, but the overall composition must remain carefully balanced and gallery-clean.
palette: Sea-glass green, faded indigo, raffia straw, red laterite, palm-kernel black, sandstone ochre, chalk white, dull brass, oxidised copper, shell cream, sparrow umber, goldfinch yellow, restrained crimson and gull-grey.
mood: Warm, tactile, watchful and quietly animated; summer heat softened by cool northern light, with a sense of dry fibre, faint bells, long shadows and salt-polished surfaces.

creative_brief.style_guidance: Develop 'Raffia Oracle of the Dry Lagoon' into a landscape-format contemporary textile-assemblage conceived as a suspended ritual frieze rather than a picture of birds. The work should feel tactile, percussive and sun-dried, with seven bird-oracle forms emerging from raffia, shell, bead, brass and stitched pigment. Keep the inherited language of raffia curtains, calabash, cowrie, recycled plastic tassels and indigo cloth, but refine it for a premium interior: spacious, deliberate, asymmetrical and materially elegant. The North Shields atmosphere should enter quietly through cool sea-glass greens, pale shell whites, weathered-sandstone ochres and salt-worn grey shadows, not through literal coastal scenery.
creative_brief.curator_notes: Today's exhibition should read as an artwork first: a wide hanging field of divinatory bird presences, arranged like a low summer wind passing through market relics, shrine fragments and harbour-worn materials. The birds are not illustrated in a naturalistic setting; they are translated into recognisable ceremonial silhouettes, charms and masks. Preserve calm despite the percussive materiality: the piece should rustle visually but not shout. The most memorable bird should be immediately legible from across the room, while the others reward slower looking through colour, weight, bead rhythm and symbolic construction.
creative_brief.mood: Warm, tactile, watchful and quietly animated; summer heat softened by cool northern light, with a sense of dry fibre, faint bells, long shadows and salt-polished surfaces.
creative_brief.visual_language: A landscape hanging composed of uneven vertical raffia falls, braided palm-rib rails, stitched indigo cotton panels and suspended bird-oracle clusters. Forms should be simplified into crests, breast patches, wings, tails and beaks using shells, beads, seed pods and metal discs. Use negative space between hanging columns so the artwork breathes. Edges should be fringed, knotted and imperfect, but the overall composition must remain carefully balanced and gallery-clean.
creative_brief.palette: Sea-glass green, faded indigo, raffia straw, red laterite, palm-kernel black, sandstone ochre, chalk white, dull brass, oxidised copper, shell cream, sparrow umber, goldfinch yellow, restrained crimson and gull-grey.
creative_brief.composition: A wide horizontal frieze with a shallow upper suspension line and long descending raffia curtains of varied lengths. The heaviest mass sits slightly below centre, grounding the work, while lighter tassels and shell forms rise toward the upper right. Seven bird-oracle zones are distributed asymmetrically across the field: low paired bundles at the left, a compact jewel-like cluster near the upper middle, a narrow vibrating strip crossing the centre, a brass-and-black charm to the right, a pale crest high in the composition and a broad calabash-cowrie body anchoring the lower centre. Leave generous quiet gaps so the Frame screen reads as a refined textile installation rather than a crowded collage.
creative_brief.bird_integration: Represent every observed bird as a recognisable stylised presence within the assemblage. European Goldfinch should be the most immediately identifiable at normal viewing distance: a compact bead-and-shell bird with a clear red facial mask, yellow wing flash, black cap and pale body, suspended like a precious oracle token. Common Wood Pigeon becomes the largest grounded form: a soft grey-lilac calabash body with a pale neck crescent made from cowries and muted green-purple bead iridescence. Yellow-legged Gull appears as a high pale shell-and-recycled-plastic crest with long angular wings, cool grey back, white head and discreet yellow leg-strips. Great Tit is a paired brass-and-black charm with a bright yellow cotton breast panel, black central stripe, white cheek discs and olive edging. Common Chiffchaff is a slim green-brown vibrating strip of beads and raffia, with a fine pointed beak and pale eye-line suggested by a single stitched thread. House Sparrow and Eurasian Tree Sparrow form twin low seed-pod bundles: the House Sparrow warmer and dustier with a grey crown and black bib tab, the Tree Sparrow neater with a chestnut cap, white cheek and small black cheek mark. All birds should remain visible as birds through silhouette, beak direction, wing rhythm and key field marks, even while transformed into ceremonial assemblage.
creative_brief.materials: Dyed raffia cascades, braided palm ribs, carved calabash segments, cowrie shells, recycled plastic strip tassels, glass trade beads, brass bottle-cap discs, hammered copper bells, indigo-starched cotton, red laterite pigment, charcoal rubbings, palm-kernel black, stitched leather tabs, seed pods, linen cord, shell fragments, dull metal wire and weathered wood-toned supports.
creative_brief.visual_focus: The viewer should first be drawn to the central gravity of the hanging field: the dense meeting of calabash, cowrie, raffia shadow and muted metallic glints against cooler indigo gaps, creating a strong tactile centre before individual forms resolve.

movement_options.name: Phosphor Dawn: The Song-Spectrum Theatre
movement_options.creative_direction: A black-box electronic media exhibition where the seven summer birds are translated into luminous acoustic identities: House Sparrow as clipped rhythmic ticks, Common Wood Pigeon as a deep pulsing bass halo, Eurasian Tree Sparrow as paired metronomic sparks, European Goldfinch as a glittering treble scatter, Common Chiffchaff as a repeated oscillating line, Yellow-legged Gull as a long torn signal, and Great Tit as a clean two-note graphic emblem. The mood is nocturnal, analytic, charged and urban, as if a dawn chorus had been captured inside an oscilloscope.
movement_options.materials: Phosphor-green OLED strips, low-resolution LED matrices, black acoustic felt, perforated speaker mesh, recycled circuit-board fragments, e-ink annotation tabs, matte carbon composite panels, copper traces, subwoofer cones, moire interference screens, ultraviolet ink, solder-bright pinpoints and programmable waveform projection.
movement_options.composition: Landscape format conceived as a panoramic spectrogram. A dense low band of sparrow pulses runs along the bottom edge; the Wood Pigeon expands as a broad circular frequency bloom left of centre; the Chiffchaff repeats across the middle as precise wave peaks; the Gull cuts diagonally through the upper register as a stretched white-noise flare. Goldfinch, Great Tit and Tree Sparrow appear as sharper coloured signal clusters punctuating the field. Large areas of matte black silence separate the signals, making the work feel spacious rather than visually noisy.
movement_options.why_it_is_distinct: This is an electronic sound-image environment, not a craft, mineral, ceramic, textile or painterly language. Its identity comes from signal, frequency, darkness, circuitry and acoustic abstraction.

movement_options.name: Sugar Tides of the Aviary Banquet
movement_options.creative_direction: A museum-grade ephemeral confectionery installation in which today's birds become courtly guests at a strange summer dessert table. The atmosphere is lush, fragile, playful and faintly decadent: the birds are not illustrated as wildlife but staged as edible heraldic presences in spun sweetness, crystallised air and melting colour.
movement_options.materials: Blown sugar domes, poured isomalt sheets, pulled sugar ribbons, pastillage plaques, wafer-paper feathers, meringue foam, candied fennel stems, crystallised citrus peel, pistachio praline dust, raspberry lake glaze, burnt caramel veining, edible pearl lustre, saffron syrup stains, poppy-seed speckling and tiny sheets of edible gold.
movement_options.composition: A horizontal banquet plateau with three rising confectionery tiers. The Common Wood Pigeon occupies the largest translucent sugar dome near the rear as a soft mauve-grey volume. The Yellow-legged Gull is a high white meringue arc spanning the upper table line. House Sparrow and Eurasian Tree Sparrow perch as small caramel-and-seed forms along the front ledge. The Goldfinch appears as a sharp saffron, black and red sugar medallion; the Chiffchaff is almost hidden in candied fennel stems; the Great Tit is a compact yellow-black pastillage badge on the central tier. Drips, crystals and shadows create a theatrical still-life rather than a natural scene.
movement_options.why_it_is_distinct: Its material imagination is edible, translucent, unstable and Rococo. No other proposal uses taste, melting, banquet structure or confectionery fragility as the primary exhibition language.

movement_options.name: Wycinanki Thunder Meadow
movement_options.creative_direction: A contemporary Slavic paper-cut movement using folk symmetry, scissor virtuosity and flat chromatic force to turn summer birds into emblems of communal weather. The emotional atmosphere is festive, sharp-edged, loud and graphic, like a village meadow transformed into a monumental cut-paper altar.
movement_options.materials: Hand-cut dyed papers, saturated tissue layers, black silhouette card, fluorescent poster stock, archival wheat paste, pin-pricked perforations, embossed paper veins, folded-paper registration creases, floating shadowbox spacers, matte white backing board and varnished paper edges.
movement_options.composition: Landscape format organised around a central mirrored meadow-tree, but deliberately interrupted so the symmetry feels contemporary rather than nostalgic. The two sparrows form paired cut silhouettes in the lower grasses; the Wood Pigeon is a large rounded blue-grey paper mass embedded in the left canopy; the Goldfinch becomes a red-yellow rosette at the centre; the Chiffchaff is a tiny repeated green notch along one branch; the Gull is reduced to a white angular slash across the top; the Great Tit is a bold yellow-black medallion balancing the right side. Negative spaces cut through the paper become as important as the coloured forms.
movement_options.why_it_is_distinct: This proposal is flat, frontal, folkloric and scissor-built. Its power comes from cut voids, folk symmetry and saturated paper rather than surface depth, precious materials, optics or architectural mass.

movement_options.name: Raffia Oracle of the Dry Lagoon
movement_options.creative_direction: A performative West African contemporary assemblage in which the birds appear as divinatory presences suspended between masquerade, marketplace colour and summer heat. The atmosphere is percussive, tactile, sun-dried and animate, as if the exhibition might rustle, clack and breathe when visitors pass.
movement_options.materials: Dyed raffia cascades, braided palm ribs, carved calabash segments, cowrie shells, recycled plastic strip tassels, glass trade beads, brass bottle-cap discs, indigo-starched cotton, red laterite pigment, charcoal rubbings, palm-kernel black, stitched leather tabs, seed pods and small hammered copper bells.
movement_options.composition: A large vertical-hanging field rather than a framed picture. Long raffia curtains descend in uneven columns, opening around seven bird-oracle zones. The Wood Pigeon is the heaviest calabash-and-cowrie mass near the lower centre; the Gull is a high pale shell-and-plastic crest; the Goldfinch is a compact red-yellow bead cluster; the Great Tit is a brass-and-black paired charm; the Chiffchaff is a narrow vibrating strip of green beads; the two sparrows appear as twin low seed-pod bundles. The composition is asymmetrical, weighted by gravity and activated by fringe, shadow and implied movement.
movement_options.why_it_is_distinct: Unlike the other movements, this is a hanging performative assemblage built from rustle, weight, bead rhythm, shell sound and masquerade energy. It is neither pictorial, digital, edible nor paper-flat.

movement_options.name: Cryo-Pop Taxonomy: Inflatable Field Station
movement_options.creative_direction: A buoyant pop-scientific installation where the seven birds are reimagined as pressurised summer specimens inside a soft laboratory of air. The atmosphere is cool, comic, synthetic and weightless, with taxonomy treated as inflatable architecture rather than documentation.
movement_options.materials: Translucent TPU membranes, heat-welded vinyl seams, helium micro-bladders, pearlescent Mylar patches, nylon valve collars, soft silicone feet, airbrushed gradient films, gel-filled portholes, zippered inspection seams, flexible printed labels, magnetic valve caps, cloudy polyurethane tubing and suspended clear monofilament.
movement_options.composition: Landscape format arranged as a row of floating specimen pods inside a pale field-station grid. Each bird receives a different inflated volume: the Wood Pigeon is an oversized soft grey bladder, the Gull a long white glider-tube near the top, the Goldfinch a taut red-yellow capsule, the Great Tit a compact yellow sphere with black seam lines, the Chiffchaff a small olive-green pressure cell, and the two sparrows a pair of tan linked pods hovering near the lower edge. The background is sparse and clinical, with faint measuring ticks and valve diagrams offset by playful bulging forms.
movement_options.why_it_is_distinct: This movement is pneumatic, synthetic and pop-taxonomic. Its visual language is air pressure, seams, valves, soft volume and laboratory absurdity, completely separate from sound media, confectionery, folk cutting or ritual assemblage.

structured_prompt.title: Raffia Oracle of the Dry Lagoon
structured_prompt.subject: A premium contemporary landscape-format textile assemblage: a suspended ritual frieze of seven stylised bird-oracle presences emerging from raffia, shell, bead, brass, calabash, stitched cloth and harbour-worn materials. The work should read first as an elegant gallery textile installation rather than a bird illustration, with each bird translated into ceremonial silhouette, charm, mask, crest or bundle while remaining recognisable through key field marks.
structured_prompt.composition: Wide horizontal frieze with a shallow upper suspension line, braided palm-rib rails and long uneven descending raffia curtains of varied lengths. Use generous negative space between vertical hanging columns so the artwork breathes. The strongest visual gravity sits slightly below centre: a dense meeting of calabash, cowrie, raffia shadow, indigo gaps and muted metallic glints. Arrange seven asymmetrical bird-oracle zones across the field: twin low seed-pod bundles at the left for House Sparrow and Eurasian Tree Sparrow; a compact jewel-like European Goldfinch cluster near the upper middle as the most immediately legible bird; a narrow vibrating Common Chiffchaff strip crossing the centre; a brass-and-black Great Tit charm to the right; a high pale Yellow-legged Gull crest with angular wings; and a broad Common Wood Pigeon calabash-cowrie body anchoring the lower centre. Lighter tassels, shell fragments and recycled plastic strips rise toward the upper right. Edges should be fringed, knotted and imperfect, but the overall balance must feel spacious, deliberate and gallery-clean.
structured_prompt.materials: Dyed raffia cascades, braided palm ribs, carved calabash segments, cowrie shells, shell fragments, glass trade beads, seed pods, recycled plastic strip tassels, brass bottle-cap discs, dull brass charms, hammered copper bells, oxidised copper wire, indigo-starched cotton panels, stitched linen cord, stitched leather tabs, red laterite pigment, charcoal rubbings, palm-kernel black pigment and weathered wood-toned supports. Surfaces should feel tactile, sun-dried, salt-worn, rustling and percussive, with visible knots, stitch marks, fibre shadows, bead rhythm and hand-assembled dimensionality.
structured_prompt.lighting: Soft northern coastal daylight filtered into a warm interior gallery setting. Use gentle side illumination to reveal fibre texture, shell sheen, dull metallic glints and long quiet shadows. Atmosphere should suggest summer heat softened by cool sea-glass light, not dramatic weather. No literal coastline or seascape; the North Shields reference should appear only through cool grey shadows, shell whites, sea-glass greens and weathered sandstone tones.
structured_prompt.colour: Sea-glass green, faded indigo, raffia straw, red laterite, palm-kernel black, sandstone ochre, chalk white, shell cream, dull brass, oxidised copper, sparrow umber, gull grey, soft grey-lilac, muted green-purple iridescence, goldfinch yellow and restrained crimson. Keep saturation refined and sun-dried; avoid bright tropical cliché. Balance warm straw, ochre and umber against cool indigo, sea-glass green and salt-grey shadows.
structured_prompt.bird_strategy: Represent all seven birds as stylised ceremonial assemblage forms, not naturalistic wildlife. European Goldfinch must be most immediately identifiable from across the room: compact bead-and-shell oracle token with clear red facial mask, black cap, pale body and a bright yellow wing flash. Common Wood Pigeon is the largest grounded form: broad soft grey-lilac calabash body, pale cowrie neck crescent and subtle muted green-purple bead iridescence. Yellow-legged Gull appears high in the composition as a pale shell-and-recycled-plastic crest with long angular wings, cool grey back, white head and discreet yellow leg strips. Great Tit becomes a paired brass-and-black charm with bright yellow cotton breast panel, black central stripe, white cheek discs and olive edging. Common Chiffchaff is a slim green-brown vibrating strip of beads and raffia with a fine pointed beak and a pale eye-line made from a single stitched thread. House Sparrow and Eurasian Tree Sparrow form twin low seed-pod bundles: House Sparrow warmer, dustier and looser with grey crown and black bib tab; Eurasian Tree Sparrow neater with chestnut cap, white cheek and small black cheek mark. All birds must remain visible as birds through silhouette, beak direction, wing rhythm, crest or breast shape and key field marks while still feeling transformed into ritual textile objects.
structured_prompt.mood: Warm, tactile, watchful and quietly animated. The piece should feel like a low summer wind passing through market relics, shrine fragments, raffia curtains and harbour-worn materials: visually rustling but calm, refined and contemplative. It should convey dry fibre, faint bells, salt-polished surfaces, long shadows and a sense of quiet divination.
